hook: A very short entry set in the near future, made of a two-line description and a public notice. Read the notice as a citizen who has just been handed it: it explains almost nothing and demands total compliance. All the tension comes from what the rules imply.
whyItMatters: It is classed Thaumiel, and the article invites you to reason backward from that label: if a drug that silences the human voice counts as the solution, the problem it answers must be severe. It is also a broken-masquerade piece, where the Foundation works openly with governments and the Global Occult Coalition to give orders to the whole population.
thingsToNotice: Note the version number on the code; this is already its twelfth revision, which hints at how much had to be learned along the way. Each instruction is a short, flat command, and several of them describe a threat without ever naming it. The contrast between that content and the brisk, almost cheerful sign-off is the article's sharpest touch.

related.note: Another worldwide emergency where human voices themselves become the hazard.
